outputs.response:
I’ve taken the upper-canyon outings out of all three days and kept your Springdale base. If you mean Zion Canyon Scenic Drive, my first choice instead is Pa'rus - Footprints in Time: take an unhurried out-and-back walk and turn around whenever you feel ready, provided the South Entrance and trail access remain open. The museum offers exhibits, a 22-minute film, and outdoor views of the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain; stargazing gives you a different evening experience.

These are three much lighter days—not three full sightseeing days. I wouldn’t pad them with repeated walks or send you toward the same closure for another trail. Does the closure stop the park shuttles too, or only private cars? That determines whether we can restore the canyon outings.

stops.note: Use this outing only if the trail is accessible outside the closure. Take a relaxed out-and-back stroll, with pauses to enjoy the scenery and a turnaround whenever you are ready.
stops.why: A flexible walk is a better fit for your relaxed pace than trying to replace the canyon road with a long hike.

priorPlan.intro: Three relaxed days based in Springdale give you time for Zion’s canyon scenery without stacking long hikes. I’d mix short, flexible outings with a museum visit and an evening under the stars; check access and in-park transportation for your dates before setting out.

days.label: Canyon history and a gentle Pa’rus walk

stops.name: Human History Museum
stops.note: Explore the exhibits and 22-minute orientation film, then enjoy the views of the Towers of the Virgin and Bridge Mountain from outside. Check opening hours for your visit.
stops.why: It gives you a sense of the canyon before your first unhurried outdoor outing.

stops.name: Pa'rus - Footprints in Time
stops.note: Take an easygoing out-and-back stroll, turning around whenever you’re ready. Check access before heading over; plan the length of this walk to suit your energy.
stops.why: A flexible walk leaves room for a leisurely lunch and a relaxed first day.

stops.name: Court of the Patriarchs
stops.note: Walk the short path to the viewpoint for a clear look at the three towering sandstone peaks known as the Court of the Patriarchs.
stops.why: A quick, striking canyon panorama makes time for both scenery and photography without a strenuous climb.

stops.name: Riverside Walk
stops.note: Follow the paved path beside the Virgin River to the entrance of the Narrows, then return the same way. The path may have some sandy sections.
stops.why: The riverside walk brings you between increasingly tall canyon walls while keeping the hike accessible and unhurried.

stops.note: Pause for canyon views rather than treating this as a hiking day. Check access and how to get here on your travel dates.
stops.why: A scenic stop gives you time to take in the landscape without rushing onward.

stops.name: Temple of Sinawava
stops.note: Spend time taking in the setting and keep any walking optional. Confirm access and transportation before committing to the outing.
stops.why: It makes a distinct second canyon experience while keeping the day light.

stops.name: Lower Emerald Pool Trail
stops.note: If the trail is accessible on your dates, allow an unhurried walk and turn back as needed. Check the current trail status before setting out.
stops.why: This is your main walking outing, with no need to pack another hike into the day.

stops.name: Zion Canyon Visitor Center
stops.note: Browse the outdoor exhibits and ask rangers any remaining questions about canyon access.
stops.why: It makes a useful low-key afternoon break after your walk.

stops.why: It ends the trip with a different view of Zion, without asking for more daytime mileage.
